title: Dynamic reservation pool and model foresight for OOM mitigation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Recent production incidents show intermittent OOMs under mixed-latency workloads despite existing KV evictions and model fallbacks. Root cause analysis points to bursty KV growth combined with aggressive batching admission that does not account for short-term KV retention spikes (e.g., long chat contexts followed by many short requests).

Goal: Implement a memory-aware admission layer + lightweight resident reservation pool ("memory reservoir") that preserves critical KV pages and gracefully degrades batching and model fidelity before triggering OOM or hard fallbacks. Add a predictive 'model foresight' heuristic to pick fallback variants proactively when a request sequence is likely to push memory beyond safe thresholds.

Proposed approach (high level):
- Admission Controller: enhance batch admission logic to consult a dynamic reservation pool and recent KV growth rate. New admission API returns one of: accept, accept-reduced (force slim batch or reduced prefetch), defer (queue with token), or reject-with-fallback.
- Memory Reservoir: maintain a small GPU-resident reservation pool (a soft quota) that is allocated from idle capacity during low usage and can be reclaimed with cooperative eviction. Reservoir size is driven by a rolling percentile of recent peak KV footprints per GPU (configurable alpha).
- Model Foresight Heuristic: runtime uses short-term sequence forecasting (based on last N requests in this slot) to predict near-term KV growth and select a model variant upfront (full model, quantized-slim, or token-limited). This reduces mid-request model swaps and costs of reactive fallback.
- Host-backed snapshots: for larger KV pages flagged as low-reuse, snapshot to host RAM asynchronously so they can be restored if needed instead of being fully dropped, enabling faster retries without a cold start.
- Retry and backoff policy: introduce fast retry with progressive degradation (first retry with reduced batch, second with slim model, third routes to fallback model or queued execution). Include per-request tracing to connect admission decisions to eventual success/failure.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller returns deterministic decision within 500us for 99% of requests
OOM incidents attributable to KV spikes reduced by >= 90% in mixed workloads (bench vs baseline)
End-to-end 95th latency regression <= 15% on production-like throughput when reservoir is active
Model foresight correctly predicts need for fallback variant for >= 85% of sequences that previously caused memory pressure
Host-backed snapshot restore latency median < 35ms for small segments and < 250ms for large segments
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha K: Created ticket after incident post-migration to new batching kernel. Linked to ENG-33000 (incident) and initial postmortem.

2026-03-03 - Diego M: Spike experiments show KV footprint percentiles vary widely between slots. Proposal: reservoir based on 90th percentile of recent peaks; using 99th causes too conservative headroom.
2026-03-05 - Design review: agreed on admission-return codes and fast-path decision budget (<=500us). Decided to keep reservoir soft so it cooperates with existing evictor rather than preempting it.
2026-03-07 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1783 implements controller stubs and metrics (WIP). Initial microbench shows <=0.3ms decision overhead.

2026-03-09 - Bench results: mixed chat workload reduced OOM rate from 12/day to 1/day in staging with reservoir=6% GPU mem; 95th latency increased 9% — within target. Need longer soak and diverse models.

2026-03-11 - Security note: host-backed snapshots touch non-sensitive transient tensors only. Confirmed with security that no customer PII persists; final design will document KMS boundaries for Private deploys.
2026-03-12 - Next: integrate model foresight heuristic with model registry to pick quantized-slim variants; schedule canary for runtime-1.22 in us-west-2 on dedicated pool.
